title: Introduce temporal attenuator and stratified cooldown guard for noisy transient regressions
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Continuous canary detectors are sensitive to short-lived, high-variance spikes that lead to noisy rollbacks and developer fatigue. This PR adds a Temporal Attenuator that reduces sensitivity to transient single-window spikes by combining multi-window consensus and an adaptive cooldown policy. It also introduces a Stratified Cooldown Guard that applies cooldowns per traffic slice (user-agent, request-size-bucket, and routing-key) rather than globally to avoid correlated false-positives across orthogonal dimensions.

Summary of changes (single string): - New detector: Temporal Attenuator (temporal_attenuator.go + unit tests) implements a lightweight EWMA + multi-window percentile voting scheme with confidence weights derived from sample counts and variance; includes a probabilistic cooldown backoff to avoid oscillation. - Stratified cooldown controller (cooldown_controller.go) that maintains cooldown state keyed by a stratification fingerprint and exposes a pluggable policy interface. - Router changes (router_integration.go) to consult stratified cooldowns before routing canary traffic and to emit per-strata metrics/tags. - Config: new canary.policy.temporal_attenuator config and canary.cooldown.strata config with sensible defaults + example in perf-canary/examples/cooldown_config.yaml. - Observability: added metrics and histograms (attenuator_vote_total, cooldown_active_strata, strata_sample_count) and dashboard snippet. - E2E synthetic test harness update to support per-strata injection and validation. - Documentation: perf-canary/docs/temporal-attenuator.md with guidance and rollout checklist.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for core attenuator voting logic - [x] Integration tests for router+cooldown interactions - [x] CI benchmarks (micro-bench) to ensure latency impact <1ms p95 on the hot path - [x] Docs + rollout example - [x] Feature flagged behind canary.experimental.temporal_attenuator

Why this is different: Most existing guards operate on global aggregated signals and either average-away real regressions or create noisy failures on high-cardinality traffic. The temporal attenuator intentionally blends opinionated short, medium, and long windows with a confidence-weighted consensus and an exponential cooldown backoff per-stratum. This preserves sensitivity to real regressions that persist across windows while attenuating one-off flukes.

Operational notes: Default config aims to be conservative: require majority positive votes from at least two windows and minimum sample counts per stratum; cooldown starts at 1 minute and doubles until a cap (default 64 minutes). Toggle via feature flag and use the example config to map meaningful strata for your workload.

Related: ENG-1209 (reduce canary churn), ENG-1217 (per-strata routing analytics).

review_comments: Rajiv Menon: Nice approach. Please add a short note on how this interacts with existing burst-protection gates; could the cooldown shadow them?

Maya Chen: Reply: The attenuator consults burst-protection first; cooldowns are per-stratum and we explicitly exclude internal burst-probe markers from cooldown state. Added a comment in router_integration.go explaining the ordering.
Sofia Alvarez: Request changes: add a safety net that prevents cooldowns from applying to < 0.1% of traffic globally (to avoid starving small but critical routes).
Maya Chen: Reply: Added a global-minimum-traffic-percent config and a unit test covering the threshold.
merge_outcome: merged via squash-merge into main; PR closed after green CI and 2 approvals
release_notes: Add temporal attenuator and stratified cooldown guard to perf-canary; feature gated behind canary.experimental.temporal_attenuator. Provides multi-window consensus and per-strata cooldowns to reduce false-positive canary rollbacks.
notes_for_oncall: If toggled on cluster-wide, monitor attenuator_vote_total and cooldown_active_strata. Watch for large numbers of tiny strata entering cooldown — consider increasing strata aggregation or raising min-samples-per-stratum.
